per_claim.no_dataset_reason: The test needs population-level whole-genome or mitogenome data for many dogs and several wild canids. The most obvious single NCBI resource, the dog reference assembly, is one genome and cannot decide the question. I tried to check the NCBI Datasets landing page for it, but the fetch was blocked by a browser-verification page, so I could not confirm it. I am not confident of the exact URL or DOI of any multi-sample resequencing dataset, such as published dog and wolf VCFs on Dryad or in the European Variation Archive. Under the no-fabrication rule I am returning null instead of guessing an identifier.

per_claim.no_dataset_reason: I could not identify, with confidence in its exact title, DOI or URL, a public dataset of sunflower capitulum seed or floret centre coordinates or parastichy crossing angles. Such a dataset would need per-seed positions in a single disc. Public sunflower data I know of are genomic, phenotypic or agronomic, not disc geometry. Specimen portals such as MorphoSource, iDigBio and GBIF do not reliably hold standardized capitulum images or coordinates. Under the no-fabrication rule, an honest null is the right answer here. The test could be run on new photographs of capitula with seed centres digitised.

It would need calibrated 3D volumetric reconstructions of isotonic and hypotonic human red blood cells, with downloadable image stacks or meshes. Candidates such as the Cell Image Library, the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection and MorphoSource were not checked for matching RBC 3D data. Naming one from memory would risk a fabricated identifier, so I am returning null.
